## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Dhammataṇhānadukkhasamudayotikathā* (Kv 13.10) is a debate located in the thirteenth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text concerns the controversial thesis that craving for mental phenomena or mind-objects is not the origin of suffering (*dhammataṇhā na dukkhasamudayo ti*) [Dube 1980]. In modern scholarship, it is cited in the context of psychological and ethical controversies among the early Buddhist schools [Dube 1980]. SuttaCentral notes one translation into a modern language and cross-references the debate to the analysis of craving in the *Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta* (DN 22) as well as the immediately preceding section, the *Dhammataṇhāabyākatātikathā* (Kv 13.9) [SuttaCentral].
According to DharmaNexus, the text exhibits substantial internal reuse across 16 Pali texts, comprising 160 matching segments [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive overlap is with the preceding debate, Kv 13.9, which shares 19 matches and 4,436 characters (spanning segments §§1.4–7.7) [DharmaNexus]. Additional textual parallels and formulaic overlaps within the canon include the *Rāhula Saṁyutta* (SN 18), the *Khandha Saṁyutta* (SN 22), the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* (Ds 2.2.2 and Ds 2.2.3), the *Saccavibhaṅga* (Vb 4), multiple other sections of the *Kathāvatthu* (such as Kv 11.4, Kv 13.3, Kv 14.7, Kv 15.11, Kv 16.10, and Kv 20.1), and commentary literature including the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Dukanipāta-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records machine-generated cross-linguistic alignments with Sanskrit works like the *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, Tibetan translations such as the *Abhidharmakośaṭīkālakṣaṇānusāriṇī* (D4093-2) and the *Pramāṇavārttikālaṃkāra* (D4221), and Chinese Āgama and canonical texts including the *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) and the *Yuanqi jing* (T 124) [DharmaNexus].
